key_insight: Concentrated attention-head dropout disrupts autoregressive reasoning more than diffuse dropout with the same cumulative masking budget.
engineering_relevance: Fault-tolerance testing for transformer inference should assess disruption concentration, not just overall dropout rates.
method: Evaluated 250 paired GSM8K derivations in Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct.
Compared clustered attention-head masking with budget-matched diffuse dropout and stratified temporal redistribution.
Explored single-step density versus multi-token continuity in a separate 100-example factorial evaluation.
evidence_signal: At onset parameter B=0.10, scheduling approximately 5.7% of vulnerable head-token volume, burst versus diffuse dropout reduced accuracy from 91.2% to 78.8% in Qwen (−12.4 pp; p=5.5×10⁻⁶) and from 84.0% to 76.8% in LLaMA (−7.2 pp; p=0.0198).
watch_item: Evidence is limited to two 8B models on GSM8K; the exploratory continuity effect was inconclusive, and some LLaMA losses involved missing final-answer formatting.
paper_title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
